To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a dengue virus inhibitory peptide induces release of the RNA genome from the virus particles.
a peptide inhibitor of dengue and related flavivirus infectivity, DN59, causes release of the viral genome from the viral particle.
the peptide, DN59 interacts directly with dengue virus to cause the release of its genome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of the peptide inhibitor of dengue and related flavivirus infections.
the development of a peptide-based inhibitor of dengue and other flavivirus infections.
the identification of novel anti-viral agents for dengue and other flavivirides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DN59 is a potent inhibitor of flaviviruses and that its mode of action is to induce release of viral genomic RNA from the virus particle.
DN59 is a potent inhibitor of flavivirus infectivity that acts by disrupting flavivirus particles and causing release of the genomic RNAs.
the DN59 peptide inhibits flaviviruses by inducing release of the RNA genome from the virus particle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the peptide, DN59 interacts with dengue virus to release its genome.
the peptide DN59 is a potent, broad spectrum inhibitor of all four serotypes and other flavivirides.
we have identified a peptide that can inhibit dengue virus infection by causing the release of the genomic viral RNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a small amphipathic peptide is capable of interacting directly with the virus particles and inducing genome release.
we have discovered a novel class of anti-dengue compounds that act on the virion itself to release the RNA genome, thereby preventing the infection of cells.
DN59 inhibits dengue virus infectivity by interacting with viral particles and inducing the release of genomic RNA from the virus particles.
